PreToolUse._comment: The check-stage evidence recorder. Separate from the guard above and non-overlapping with it: read tools never reach that matcher, so a REVIEW stage — whose work is almost entirely reading — would leave an empty proof-of-work ledger and have every honest PASS rejected. Widening the guard's matcher instead would put every file read inside a default-deny security guard's blast radius; recording has the opposite failure preference, so it gets its own hook. This one only ever allows.

No stage may ask the human: a drive is unattended between the plan gate and the ship gate, so a question dialog opened mid-VERIFY stalls the run on someone who may not be at the terminal. The shipped agents exclude the ask tool in their `tools:` enumeration, but that only covers the agents THIS repo ships — an agent added to a consuming repo's own workflow kind inherits every tool the host offers, and no other matcher here can see this one. Marker-gated, so an ordinary session asks freely; its own hook rather than a branch in the guard above because that one fails CLOSED on an unknown host, which here would refuse a HUMAN's question over a typo'd env var.

Separate from the guard above, and deliberately non-overlapping with it: no alternative in that matcher is a substring of Agent or Task, so no call is ever seen by both hooks. Two PreToolUse hooks returning updatedInput for the same call is undocumented behaviour. The split also keeps the policies apart — the guard fails CLOSED on an unknown host, this one fails OPEN.

The spawn-stage guard: this host has no driver, so an orchestrating model owns workflow_stage -> spawn -> workflow_advance, and skipping a call leaves the machine at VERIFY while a REVIEW subagent runs — its verdict then rejected as stage drift after a whole stage was paid for. Blocks a spawn of a stage agent the live marker has not armed. It shares the matcher above but NOT that hook's job: it only ever exits 0 or 2 and never emits an updatedInput envelope, which is the one thing two hooks on one call must not both do — that is why this is a third entry rather than more code inside the stamp. Their failure preferences are opposites too (the stamp fails open on everything; this one refuses), the same reason check-evidence is split from check-stage-guard.

PostToolUse._comment: The PLAN GATE follow-up. workflow_advance's park arm already returns a `next` line asking for the Approve/Replan/Park question, but that is prose inside data — the same thing gate-ask.mjs exists to stop being the only carrier. This re-emits it as a system reminder beside the tool result. Matches both tool ids Claude Code surfaces (the plain and the plugin-bundled alias). It only ever adds context: no decision, no block, and every uncertainty exits silently.
